program_name: Graduate Group in Nutritional Biology (GGNB) - MS and PhD in Nutritional Biology
degree_level: PhD; MS (thesis, Plan I) / MS (Plan II)
department_or_school: Graduate Group in Nutritional Biology (interdepartmental; College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences)
spring_2027_deadline: No spring admission - GGNB admissions page says admission is open for the Fall Quarter only (https://ggnb.ucdavis.edu/prospective-students/admissions)
fall_2027_deadline: 2026-12-15 priority (also prospective-student fellowship deadline); 2027-01-15 general; June 1 space-available (https://gradstudies.ucdavis.edu/programs/gnub ; https://grad.ucdavis.edu/program-application-deadlines)
funding_deadline_note: Apply by the Dec 15, 2026 priority deadline to qualify for fellowships (Graduate Studies deadlines page). International applicants should treat Dec 15 as the real deadline.
ielts_subscore_note: UC Davis Graduate Studies minimum IELTS overall band 7.0 (Academic or Indicator); scores valid 2 years. IELTS 7.5+ exempts from first-year English course requirement. Applicant's 6.5 is BELOW the minimum - retake needed.
toefl_min: 80 iBT (Admission Criteria page); newer English Language Examinations page lists 4.5 on the new 1-6 TOEFL scale
funding_summary: GGNB Financial Assistance page: 'The graduate program goal for doctoral student funding is to provide a living salary or stipend... often paid as a combination of GSR, Teaching Assistant, Work Study or Fellowship(s).' TA positions 'cover the cost of your in-state tuition, most fees' and pay a 25% or 50% FTE salary. Named GGNB fellowships (Kirvin Knox, Rucker Family, Mar Family). Funding for MS students and coverage of nonresident supplemental tuition for international students: Not verified.
notes: Graduate Studies deadlines list says 'GRE not required or accepted' for Nutritional Biology (a 2020 GGNB PDF said GRE recommended but not required - superseded). MS Plan I and PhD applicants are expected to contact faculty whose research fits and ask about willingness to accept a new student before the deadline; Plan II MS applicants do not need a major professor. The 2027-28 application opened mid-to-late Sept 2026. IELTS 7.0 minimum makes this a poor fit unless the applicant retakes IELTS.

program_name: Master of Advanced Study (MAS) in Maternal and Child Nutrition
department_or_school: Department of Nutrition, with UC Davis Continuing and Professional Education
spring_2027_deadline: No spring admission - admission is for fall quarter only (https://nutrition.ucdavis.edu/academics/grad-programs/mcn/how-to-apply)
fall_2027_deadline: Not verified - Fall 2027 dates not yet posted; program page says Fall 2027 applications open in October 2026. The application page listed priority Feb 15, general Apr 15 and space-available Jun 1 for the (now closed) Fall 2026 cycle (https://nutrition.ucdavis.edu/academics/grad-programs/mcn/how-to-apply)
ielts_subscore_note: 7.0 is the UC Davis Graduate Studies campus-wide minimum for graduate study (applications go through Graduate Studies); a program-specific English requirement was not checked. Applicant's 6.5 is below it.
toefl_min: 80 iBT (UC Davis Admission Criteria page; newer page lists 4.5 on the 1-6 TOEFL scale)
funding_summary: Self-supporting program of 36 units of coursework; program site listed tuition of $654/unit for 2024-2025 (may be outdated). No assistantship, waiver or stipend information seen - not a funded option.
notes: POOR FIT for a funded F-1 applicant; recorded only because of the maternal and child nutrition focus. Part-time program designed for working professionals: classes meet 2 nights a week for 6 quarters (2 years). F-1 status normally requires full-time enrollment; whether this program can issue an I-20 is Not verified. Minimum GPA 3.0; prerequisites listed: one year general chemistry, two quarters organic chemistry, statistics, one course in general physiology, two quarters nutritional biochemistry. Materials: CV/resume, statement of purpose, personal statement, three recommenders, unofficial transcripts; applications through UC Davis Graduate Studies. Department phone (530) 754-5364.
